To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Procedural justice mediates the effect of police encounter on police legitimacy, (2) Personal sense of power is the causal mediator in the effect of procedural injustice on police and legal legitmacy, (3) Police legitimacy mediates the effect on legal compliance, (4) Normative alignment mediates the effect o police legitimacy on willingness cooperate with the police, and (5) Police legitimacy and normative alignment have different psychological drivers.

procedural justice is the key to police legitimacy and that the psychological mechanisms through which procedural justice works are different from those posited by the dominant theories of procedural justice.

(1) procedural justice mediates, in the sense of a causal mechanism, the impact of an officer's behavior on police legitimacy, (2) personal sense of power mediates, in that same sense, the impact of procedural fairness on both police and legal legitimacy, (3) police legitimacy mediates, in a different sense, the impact on willingness to cooperate and legal compliance.

the impact of procedural fairness in policing.
the question of how to improve the quality of policing, in terms of both the quality of police-public relationships and police effectiveness.

the question of whether and how the way in which the police treat people during encounters with the police affects the legitimacy of the police, and how this in turn affects citizens' attitudes and behaviours toward the police.
